question.text: In a trust structure, the AIF does not have the ability to sue or be sued directly. Instead:

answer.text: The sponsor handles all legal matters
The trustee represents the trust in legal proceedings
No legal action is possible against the AIF

explanation.text: The Logic: A trust registered under the Indian Trusts Act 1882 does not have separate legal personality - it cannot sue or be sued in its own name. The trustee is entitled to sue or be sued for and on behalf of the trust (pp. 45, 102, 188-189). The Trap: This does not mean the trust is immune from legal action - it means legal action is taken through the trustee. Note: Additional claims about how trust assets are reached to satisfy claims, or about how to select a well-capitalised trustee, go beyond the cited workbook pages and should be separately sourced before being treated as guidance.
